best_available_evidence: Nonheterantherous floral morphology is source-resolved. Amegilla territorial behaviour was observed above water containing M. australasica, but this is not a flower visit or effective-pollination event.
notes: Do not promote territorial behaviour or comparative buzz-pollination statements into species-level effective pollination.

best_available_evidence: Equal-stamen morphology and phylogenetic placement are source-resolved, but no species-level direct flower-visitation, stigma-contact, pollen-transfer, or reproductive-effect receipt was recovered.
notes: Remain an OPEN alternative rather than infer eligibility from congeners.

best_available_evidence: Bee handling, poricidal pollen extraction, stigma contact, and isomorphic equal/subequal stamens are source-resolved. No quantitative pollen-removal versus stigma-deposition/export experiment or fitness manipulation was recovered.
notes: Morphology and descriptive visitation are insufficient for the registered pollen-fate conflict estimand.

best_available_evidence: Binary pollen-reward versus transfer conflict is POSITIVE; seven fertile poricidal stamens and buzz pollination are source-resolved, and flowers are monosymmetric. No species-specific experiment resolves positional, petal-mediated, among-flower, or genuinely shared-integrated routing.
notes: Equal or weakly differentiated morphology cannot be used to infer SHARED_INTEGRATED because S. spectabilis shows functional routing despite equal fertile-stamen morphology.

best_available_evidence: The nearest prospective Bixaceae control candidate is phylogenetically adjacent to Amoreuxia and source-resolved as lacking Amoreuxia-style dimorphic fertile-stamen sets. Searches under C. tetraporum and the synonyms C. argentinense, Maximilianea tetrapora, and M. argentinensis recovered no species-level flower-visitation, stigma-contact, pollen-transfer, or reproductive-effect source.
notes: Do not infer species-level pollination from poricidal-anther morphology or from bee pollination documented in other Cochlospermum species.
